topic: How AI Models Learn: Parameters, Training & Prediction
description: Check your understanding of parameters, forward/backward pass, loss, gradient descent, self-supervised learning, and overfitting.

questions.question: What does 'learning' mean for a neural network?
options: Downloading a dictionary of facts into memory
Adjusting parameters so future predictions improve
Copying human brain cells into silicon
questions.explanation: Learning means repeatedly modifying adjustable numbers (parameters) so the model gets better at its objective — not storing facts like human memory.

questions.question: What are parameters in a neural network?
options: The raw training documents stored on disk
Adjustable internal numbers — mainly weights and biases — tuned during training
The user's API key and rate limits
questions.explanation: Parameters are weights and biases (the 'knobs'). Training data feeds the network; parameters live inside it and get updated during training.

questions.question: Do parameters store knowledge the same way humans store facts?
options: Yes — each fact is saved in one dedicated parameter
No — they encode patterns and relationships used to process inputs
Only GPT-4 stores facts; smaller models do not
questions.explanation: Parameters encode patterns and relationships. Algorithms use them to process input and produce output — not a human-like fact database.

questions.question: What does a loss function measure?
options: How expensive the GPU rental is
How wrong a prediction is compared to the true answer
How many parameters the model has
questions.explanation: Loss converts prediction quality into a number. Correct → small loss; very wrong → large loss. Training tries to drive loss toward zero.

questions.question: What does backpropagation actually do?
options: It directly rewrites all weights to the correct answer
It calculates gradients — how changing each parameter would affect the loss
It deletes bad training examples from the dataset
questions.explanation: Backprop computes gradients. An optimization algorithm (e.g. gradient descent) then uses those gradients to update parameters.

questions.question: Which gradient descent style is the industry standard?
options: Batch Gradient Descent only
Stochastic Gradient Descent on one example only
Mini-Batch Gradient Descent on small groups of examples
questions.explanation: Mini-batch balances Batch GD's stability with SGD's speed — e.g. groups of 32 examples — and is the usual approach for modern training.

questions.question: What is an epoch?
options: One optimization update on a single batch
One complete pass through the entire training dataset
The moment inference starts after training
questions.explanation: An epoch = one full pass over the whole dataset. Models usually need many epochs. A training step is one optimization update.

questions.question: What is overfitting?
options: The model performs well on new data but poorly on training data
The model memorizes training examples and fails on new examples
The model has too few parameters to learn anything
questions.explanation: Overfitting = excellent on training data, weak on unseen data. Good learning generalizes patterns beyond exact training examples.
